The fluorescent lights of the accounting department hummed with the same energy as the panic rising in Dave’s chest. It was "Bring Your Pet to Work Day," a corporate initiative designed to boost morale by allowing employees to bring in animals that were generally not allowed in the building. Dave, a man whose idea of excitement was finding a parking spot close to the elevator, had brought in Barnaby, a African Grey Parrot with a vocabulary that exceeded his own.

Barnaby was perched on a stack of quarterly reports, his black eyes fixed on Dave with unsettling intelligence.

"Good morning, Dave," Barnaby squawked, tilting his head. "Did you file the Q3 projections?"

Dave forced a smile, adjusting his tie. "Yes, Barnaby. They’re in the server. Please be quiet."

"Server," Barnaby repeated. "Server. Server. *Click.*"

Dave froze. He had just taken a call from the CEO’s assistant, discussing the merger with a rival firm. The call had been confidential. The phone had been on speaker. Barnaby had been in the room.

"Barnaby," Dave whispered, leaning in. "No more talking about work."

"Work," Barnaby chirped. "Work. *Merger.*"

Dave’s blood ran cold. He looked around. The office was bustling. Sarah from HR was laughing at her desk. Mike from IT was typing furiously. And then, the door to the conference room opened. Mr. Henderson, the CEO, walked in, holding a cup of coffee and looking for his assistant.

"Dave," Henderson said, spotting him. "Got a minute? I need to discuss the final terms of the merger. It’s highly sensitive."

Dave’s heart hammered against his ribs. "Sure, sir. Just... give me a second."

He turned to Barnaby. "Barnaby, listen to me. If you say anything about the merger, I will never give you another sunflower seed. Do you understand?"

Barnaby puffed out his chest. "Sunflower seed. Sunflower seed. *Betrayal.*"

Dave gasped. "I didn't say betrayal!"

"You did," Barnaby said. "You said betrayal. And *insider trading.*"
